# How to Park a Car in Japan : Your Guide to Rules, Fees & Finding Spots

![](https://article-image.travel.navitime.jp/img/NTJhowto0056-en/Photo_0.jpg)

Just like driving in Japan (and countless other aspects of daily life), parking your car is fairly straightforward but involves some rules and practices that range from esoteric to common sense. Clear signage usually makes it easy enough to figure out where and when to park your vehicle, but here are some simple tips to keep in mind.

- ## Decoding Japanese Parking Signs: Your Key to Stress-Free Parking in Japan



In Japan, parking is rarely a guessing game thanks to ubiquitous signage! If on-street parking is permitted, it will be clearly marked, often including allowed times. Look for the universally recognized circled 'P' emblem for parking garages and lots. These signs will detail parking times, prices, and crucially, availability – keep an eye out for the kanji **'空'**, (kū) meaning 'Empty', or **'満'**,(man) meaning 'Full'. While deciphering all the details on parking lot signs might take a moment, it's far easier than dealing with a parking ticket from the diligent, bicycle-riding parking attendants. Pay attention to signs indicating parking hours, fees, and any specific rules, as parking violations can lead to fines.

- ## Navigating Parking Fees in Japan: Understanding Costs & Payment Methods



![Detailed Japanese parking lot sign showing various parking rates for daytime, nighttime, and maximum charges, highlighting Japan parking fees.](https://article-image.travel.navitime.jp/img/NTJhowto0056-en/Photo_1.jpg)

Detailed Japanese parking lot sign showing various parking rates for daytime, nighttime, and maximum charges, highlighting Japan parking fees.



Parking prices in Japan typically fluctuate based on the day of the week and time of day. Most lots, particularly in city centers, charge higher rates during peak daytime hours and offer lower prices during off-peak evening and overnight hours. Signs will also display the maximum charge per 24 hours (最大料金 - saidai ryōkin), which often differs between weekdays (Monday-Friday) and weekends/holidays.



**Typical Parking Rates:** Expect to pay anywhere from JPY 100 to JPY 500 per 30 minutes in central urban areas, but this can vary greatly. Some lots offer a maximum daytime rate (e.g., 8:00-20:00 for JPY 1500-2500). Overnight maximums are usually cheaper.

**Paying for Your Spot:** In multi-story parking garages, the system is often similar to elsewhere: take a ticket upon entry and pay at a machine or to an attendant before exiting. For the common automated mini-lots, payment is also straightforward. At the central payment kiosk (精算機 - seisanki), enter your parking space number, confirm the duration and amount charged, and then pay. Usual payment options include cash (coins and ¥1000 notes are widely accepted), credit cards (Visa/Mastercard often accepted, others may vary), and increasingly, IC cards (like Suica or Pasmo) or other forms of e-money. Ensure you have your payment ready. After payment, the locking mechanism for your car will disengage, allowing you to drive out.

- ## Types of Parking Lots in Japan and How to Use Them



![A typical Japanese coin parking lot with individual car barriers, illustrating a common type of parking in Japan.](https://article-image.travel.navitime.jp/img/NTJhowto0056-en/Photo_2.jpg)

A typical Japanese coin parking lot with individual car barriers, illustrating a common type of parking in Japan.



Parking lots in Japan, especially in urban areas, can be remarkably compact compared to Western standards, often utilizing small vacant plots for income generation. Many are small, holding fewer than a dozen spaces.



**Coin Parking (Flap-lock/Bar-lock Lots):** These are very common. Each space is equipped with an individual barrier (a flap or bar on the ground).

1\. Park your car fully within the designated space.

2\. After a few minutes (usually 3-5), the barrier under your car will automatically rise, locking it in place. Confirm it has risen.

3\. When you're ready to leave, go to the central payment machine.

4\. Enter your parking space number.

5\. The machine will display the fee. Pay using cash, card, or IC card as indicated. \\n6. Once payment is complete, the barrier for your space will lower. You typically have a few minutes to exit.



**Gated Parking Garages:** These are larger, often multi-story structures.

1\. Drive to the entrance gate and take a ticket from the automated dispenser. The gate will open.

2\. Find an available parking spot.

3\. Before returning to your car to leave, locate a payment kiosk (often near elevators or exits). Insert your ticket and pay the displayed fee.

4\. Retrieve your validated ticket.

5\. Drive to the exit gate, insert your validated ticket, and the gate will open.

![Plug the meter](https://article-image.travel.navitime.jp/img/NTJhowto0056-en/Photo_3.jpg)

- ## Smart Savers: Finding Deals and Free Parking in Japan



![A parking space at a Japanese shopping center, potentially eligible for free validated parking for customers.](https://article-image.travel.navitime.jp/img/NTJhowto0056-en/Photo_4.jpg)

A parking space at a Japanese shopping center, potentially eligible for free validated parking for customers.



While the concept of vast, free parking lots attached to every business isn't widespread in Japan's urban centers, there are ways to save. Outside of small towns and remote areas where driving is the norm, paid parking is common. However, look for exceptions to reduce costs. Large shopping malls, some supermarkets, electronics stores, or entertainment complexes may offer free parking to customers, often validated by making a purchase or spending a certain amount. Typically, you'll need to present your parking ticket and purchase receipt at a service counter or store cashier to get your parking validated for a few hours of free or discounted parking. Always check the conditions, as free parking time is usually limited. Planning your shopping or dining around such establishments can save you a considerable amount on parking fees, especially in expensive city areas.

- ## The Art of Reversing: Japan's Back-In Parking Culture



![A car neatly backed into a parking space in Japan, demonstrating the common practice of reverse parking.](https://article-image.travel.navitime.jp/img/NTJhowto0056-en/Photo_5.jpg)

A car neatly backed into a parking space in Japan, demonstrating the common practice of reverse parking.



You'll quickly notice that most drivers in Japan back into parking spaces. There are several reasons for this strong preference. Many believe it's safer, allowing for a clearer view when exiting into traffic. It can also be more convenient for loading/unloading luggage from the trunk, especially in tight spaces. Furthermore, in Japan's often narrow parking lots and streets, reversing in can make maneuvering easier. While not a legally enforced rule in most places, it's a deeply ingrained unwritten rule and a matter of parking etiquette. Especially when parking in a public pay lot or any shared parking area, it's highly recommended to reverse into the spot. It's simply the 'Japanese way' and shows consideration for other drivers.

- ## Finding Parking: Smart Strategies and Tools for Japan Car Parks



Finding an available parking spot, especially in popular tourist destinations or busy city centers, can be challenging. However, several tools and strategies can help.



**Parking Apps and Websites:** Numerous smartphone apps and websites provide real-time information on parking lot locations, availability, and sometimes even prices. Search for terms like 'Japan parking app' or check your car navigation system, which often includes a parking search function. Some services may even allow for advance booking, though this is less common for short-term tourist parking.

**Parking Around Train Stations:** If you're exploring a city but staying outside the center, consider parking your car near a suburban train station and using public transport to reach downtown areas. This 'Park and Ride' strategy can save you money and the stress of city driving and parking.

**Look for 'P' Signs:** As mentioned, keep a sharp eye out for the 'P' parking signs. They are your best guide. Also, many larger commercial facilities will have clear signage directing you to their parking areas.

- ## Parking in Japan's Major Cities: Tips for Navigating Tokyo, Kyoto, and Osaka



Parking in metropolises like Tokyo, Kyoto, and Osaka presents unique challenges for drivers.



**High Costs and Limited Availability:** Be prepared for higher parking fees and scarcer spots in central areas of these cities. Street parking is extremely limited and heavily regulated.

**Consider Public Transport:** These cities boast world-class public transportation systems. For sightseeing within the city centers, using trains and subways is often more efficient and economical than driving and parking.

**Strategic Parking Locations:** If driving is necessary, research parking lots on the city fringes or near your accommodation beforehand. Some hotels offer parking, but it may be limited and incur extra charges; confirm when booking.

**Time Restrictions:** Pay close attention to time restrictions. Many lots have different fee structures for daytime and nighttime, and exceeding your paid time can result in hefty additional charges or your vehicle being clamped or towed.

- ## FAQ: Parking in Japan for Tourists



Q1: What happens if I overstay my parking time in Japan?

A1: Overstaying can lead to additional charges, often at a higher rate. In some cases, especially with flap-lock parking, if you haven't paid, the barrier won't lower. For street parking or severe violations, your car might be ticketed, clamped, or even towed, leading to significant fines and recovery costs. Always check signs for penalties and pay attention to the maximum parking time allowed.



Q2: Can I use international credit cards at all parking machines in Japan?

A2: While many modern parking machines, especially in cities and at airports, accept international credit cards (Visa and Mastercard are most commonly accepted), it's not universal. Some older machines or those in rural areas might only accept cash (coins and ¥1000 notes are essential) or specific Japanese IC cards (like Suica, Pasmo). It's always wise to carry some cash as a backup for parking fees.



Q3: Are there any apps to help find and pay for parking in Japan?

A3: Yes, there are several Japanese apps designed to help find parking, such as NAVITIME Drive Supporter (though some features may be primarily in Japanese) or the Japan Travel by NAVITIME app. Some services can provide real-time availability and price comparisons. Direct payment through apps for public parking is becoming more common but isn't standard for all lots yet. Some private parking services might offer app-based booking and payment.



Q4: Is it easy to find parking at popular tourist attractions in Japan?

A4: This can vary significantly. Major tourist attractions often have dedicated parking facilities, but these can fill up quickly, especially during peak seasons (like cherry blossom season or Golden Week) and on weekends. Parking fees at popular spots can also be quite high. For attractions located in congested city centers (e.g., historical areas of Kyoto or central Tokyo), using Japan's excellent public transport is often a more convenient and economical choice. It's advisable to check the official website of the tourist attraction for specific parking information and alternatives before you go.



Q5: What should I do if the parking payment machine is only in Japanese and I don't understand it?

A5: Many newer parking payment machines in tourist areas and major cities offer an English language option; look for a button that says 「英語」, "English", or has a language selection icon. If an English option isn't available, try to identify key kanji such as 「精算」 (seisan - payment), 「番号」 (bangō - number), 「確認」 (kakunin - confirm), and 「円」 (en - yen). If you're completely stuck, look for a parking lot attendant (if available) or a posted helpline number you can call for assistance. Taking a photo of the machine and instructions to use a translation app might also be an option.

# Procedure for using time-charge parking spaces

- [Japanese](https://www.navipark1.com/sp/guide/)
- English
- [Chinese](https://www.navipark1.com/sp/guide/cn.html)

## Procedure for using the time-charge parking space

- [Procedure for using the locking-plate-type parking space](https://www.navipark1.com/sp/guide/en.html#anc01)
- [Procedure for using the gate-type parking space](https://www.navipark1.com/sp/guide/en.html#anc02)
- [Terms of use of parking spaces](https://www.navipark1.com/sp/guide/en.html#anc03)

### Procedure for using the locking-plate-type parking space

\*The procedure for using parking spaces may differ depending on the parking lot, i.e., in the case of the lockless-type parking, etc.

#### How to park

1Before driving the vehicle into the parking space, make sure that the locking plate is down and that there are no safety-related issues.![](https://www.navipark1.com/guide/images/index_il001.jpg)

2Slowly drive over the locking plate and park the vehicle.![](https://www.navipark1.com/guide/images/index_il002.jpg)

3The locking-plate will come up after a certain period of time.![](https://www.navipark1.com/guide/images/index_il003.jpg)

#### How to exit

1Enter the parking space number in the fee settlement machine, which will show the parking fee owed.

\*The user may need to press the 'enter (確認)' button, etc., after entering the parking space number, depending on the type of machine being used.![](https://www.navipark1.com/guide/images/index_il004.jpg)

2Pay the parking fee being displayed on the machine.

\*Credit card payment option is available only at certain parking lots.![](https://www.navipark1.com/guide/images/index_il005.jpg)

3After the parking fee has been paid, the locking plate will come down.

4Make sure that the locking plate has fully come down, before driving the vehicle from the parking space.

\*If the vehicle is not moved from the parking space for a certain period of time, the locking plate will come back up.![](https://www.navipark1.com/guide/images/index_il002.jpg)

### Procedure for using the gate-type parking space

\*The procedure for using parking spaces may differ depending on the parking lot, i.e., in the case of the ticketless-type parking, etc.

#### How to park

1Stop the vehicle in front of the ticket machine. Then, press the 'ticket issue (発券)' button.![](https://www.navipark1.com/guide/images/index_il006.jpg)

2When the ticket is taken, the boom gate will open.

\*Please keep the ticket in a safe place, as it will be needed to exit the parking lot.![](https://www.navipark1.com/guide/images/index_il007.jpg)

3Park the vehicle in any open parking space.

\*Be sure not to park the vehicle in a space that is reserved for monthly rental (月極) or exclusive use (専用).![](https://www.navipark1.com/guide/images/index_il008.jpg)

#### How to exit

1Stop the vehicle in front of the fee settlement machine. Then, insert the ticket into the machine.

2Pay the parking fee being displayed on the machine.

\*Credit card payment option is available only at certain parking lots.![](https://www.navipark1.com/guide/images/index_il006.jpg)

3After the parking fee has been paid, the boom gate will open. Then, the user may drive out of the parking lot.

\*Please do not back up the vehicle after passing the gate, as doing so could break the boom that comes down after the vehicle once passes it.![](https://www.navipark1.com/guide/images/index_il007.jpg)

# Terms of use of parking spaces

## CHAPTER 1　GENERAL PROVISIONS

### ARTICLE 1　FORMATION OF CONTRACT

- Each parking lot user (hereinafter referred to as the “User”) must agree to these terms before its actual use of the parking lot. These terms shall apply to the User from the time it enters into the parking facility until the time it exits the parking facility.

### ARTICLE 2　PURPOSE OF USE OF THE PARKING LOT

- Starts Amenity Corporation (hereinafter referred to as the “Administrator”) shall offer a space on the parking lot to the User for a fee pursuant to these terms.

### ARTICLE 3　PARKING FEE

- Each User of the parking lot shall be obliged to pay its parking fee for the period of time that it uses the parking lot, in the amount and pursuant to the fee schedule as indicated at the parking lot.
- The period of time that the User is deemed to have used the parking lot is defined as the sensor-detected time duration that begins when the vehicle is first parked in a parking space and ends when the vehicle is driven out of the parking space.
- The User must pay its parking fee using the fee settlement or payment machine, etc., that is installed at the parking lot. The User must settle its payment by following the specified fee settlement procedure.

### ARTICLE 4　TIME PERIOD ALLOWED FOR TIME-CHARGE USE

- The User shall be allowed to use the parking lot for a maximum of 48 consecutive hours per use (unless the User has a parking pass).


However, the above restriction does not apply, if the User has obtained the Administrator's prior permission to park its vehicle for a longer period of time due to an unavoidable reason, or if a different time restriction is indicated at the parking lot.

### ARTICLE 5　TYPES OF VEHICLES THAT ARE NOT ALLOWED TO USE THE PARKING LOT

The following types of vehicles are not allowed to use the parking lot. However, if this particular parking lot has a special designation as to what types of vehicles are allowed contrary to the following restrictions, such special designation must be followed instead.

- Vehicle restrictions by size

1. Total vehicle length: any vehicle longer than 5.0m is prohibited. Total vehicle width: any vehicle that is wider than 1.9m is prohibited. Maximum vehicle height: any vehicle that is higher than 2.1m is prohibited. Maximum load weight: any vehicle with a maximum load weight in excess of 2.0t is prohibited.Minimum ground clearance: any vehicle with a minimum ground clearance of 15cm or less is prohibited. (However, if a different restriction on the maximum vehicle height is indicated at the parking lot, it must be followed instead).

- Vehicle restrictions based on statutory violation, etc.

1. Any unregistered vehicle, vehicle with expired automobile inspection, and vehicle that is otherwise not legally allowed to be operated on public roads.
2. Any vehicle that is difficult to be identified by automated registration number recognition equipment, i.e., a vehicle with a covered or removed number plate, etc.
3. Any vehicle for which the vehicle registration number has been changed but the registration amendment procedure has not yet been officially completed.
4. Any vehicle that is otherwise difficult to identify, i.e., a vehicle that is only temporarily registered, etc.

- Vehicle restrictions from the perspective of preventing damage to other vehicles

1. Any vehicle with an attached item that could come in contact and possibly damage the parking facility, equipment, or another vehicle.
2. Any special large vehicle or construction work vehicle, etc., that could possibly damage the parking facility or equipment.
3. Any vehicle carrying a dangerous item, hazardous contaminant, or other item that could cause a safety or health hazard, offensive odor, or liquid leakage.
4. Any vehicle with carrying gear being attached that could come in contact with another vehicle, or from which a load might fall off.

- Applicability of any of the aforementioned restrictions shall be determined by also considering any equipment being attached to the vehicle, load being carried by the vehicle, etc.

- Restrictions on motorcycles, tricycles, etc.


Any motorcycles, motorized bicycles, bicycles, special small vehicles, side cars, tricycles, buggies, trikes, and the like shall not be allowed.


However, if a sign says that any of these vehicles may be parked, parking shall be allowed, provided that the User complies with the rules being posted there.

### ARTICLE 6　VEHICLE OPERATION IN THE PARKING LOT

The User must comply with the following rules when operating its vehicle inside the parking lot.

- The User must operate its vehicle at a speed of 8km/h or below, while ensuring the safety of any pedestrians, etc., that may be present in the parking lot.
- No passing is allowed.
- The User must yield to any vehicle that is pulling out of a parking space.
- If any special instruction is provided by the parking lot staff, the User must obey such instruction.

### ARTICLE 7　MATTERS THAT ARE COMPULSORY OR PROHIBITED

- The User must abide by the following rules when using the parking lot.

01. The User must check what its parking space number is, and pay the parking fee before driving the vehicle out of the parking space.
02. If the User is driving its vehicle from the parking space and it has to pay no fee due to the short length of the parking time, or a reduced fee due to a discount service, etc., the User must still settle its account using the fee settlement machine without exception.
03. The User must take with it any valuable and other belongings of significance, instead of leaving them in the vehicle.
04. The User must shut off the engine at all times when the vehicle is parked. When the User intends to leave the vehicle, it must close all windows and lock all doors and also the trunk.
05. The User must park its vehicle in a specified parking space and must not park it in any other place.
06. The User must not leave any infant alone inside the parked vehicle.
07. The User must not leave any animal behind in the parked vehicle.
08. In addition to the aforementioned restrictions, the User must obey any other instructions that the Administrator or the parking lot staff may provide.
09. Smoking and use of fire are strictly prohibited in the parking lot.
10. The User must not bring any explosive or inflammable item into the parking lot.
11. The User must not engage in any act that could be a nuisance to the people nearby, such as use of a car stereo with the volume turned up, opening and closing car doors in a rough manner, speaking in loud voice at night, etc.
12. The User must pay due attention to keeping the parking lot clean and must not litter it with glass bottles, cans, waste paper or cloth, cigarette butts, magazines, bulk trash, etc.
13. The User must not engage in any other acts besides parking its vehicle in the parking lot (which include sales activities, advertising, canvassing for donations, collecting signatures, etc.).
14. If the User has any unhygienic item being carried in or attached to its vehicle, or if there is a risk that any liquid could be discharged or spilled from its vehicle, the User shall be prohibited from bringing the vehicle into the parking lot.
15. The User must not engage in any act that could be a nuisance to others in the parking lot, such as drinking alcoholic beverages, lodging, gambling, car washing, etc.

## CHAPTER 2　DISCLAIMERS AND THE USER'S RESPONSIBILITY TO COMPENSATE FOR DAMAGE

### ARTICLE 8 DISCLAIMERS

In principle, the Administrator shall not be held responsible for a theft or loss of, or damage to, any vehicle or any item being carried by a vehicle in any of the cases as specified in (1) through (12) below.

- In principle, the Administrator shall not be held responsible for any damage suffered by a User that is caused by an act of another User of the parking lot or another person, or by another vehicle, any item attached thereto, or any item being carried thereon that exists in the parking lot:

01. refund request, etc., by the User after the User had failed to check or properly identify its parking space number and incorrectly settled the parking fee;
02. damage suffered by the User in the form of its vehicle, etc., getting damaged by the locking equipment (i.e., the flap plate or the lift) as a result of the User not properly checking to see if it was fully lowered to the ground, when entering into or exiting from the parking space;
03. damage suffered by the User in the form of a theft of its vehicle or any item being carried on, attached to, or left inside the vehicle (i.e., theft of its vehicle or any part thereof);
04. damage suffered by the User in the form of damage being caused to any modified body part that is attached to its vehicle, if any, after the User having driven such vehicle into the parking lot and the part coming into contact with any parking equipment;
05. any other type of damage suffered as a result of the User parking its vehicle in violation of ARTICLE 5 hereof;
06. damage suffered as a result of the User operating its vehicle in violation of ARTICLE 6 hereof;
07. any other type of damage suffered due to the User's own negligence;
08. damage suffered as a result of a natural disaster such as a typhoon, storm, flood, earthquake, fire, or lightning strike, or any other force majeure event;
09. damage suffered by the User in the form of time spent waiting for any unauthorized vehicle or another vehicle, etc., that prevented the User from entering into or exiting from a parking space; lost opportunity; or any other type of damage;
10. damage suffered by the User as a result of any trouble that the User became involved in with another parking lot User or a third party;
11. damage suffered by the User as a result of any action taken pursuant to ARTICLE 11 \[SUSPENSION OF PARKING LOT OPERATION, ETC.\] or ARTICLE 12 \[CHANGING OF PARKING LOCATION\] hereof; and
12. damage suffered by the User as a result of it being unable to drive its vehicle out of the parking space due to a cause that is not attributable to the Administrator or any other type of damage.

### ARTICLE 9　THE USER'S RESPONSIBILITY TO COMPENSATE FOR DAMAGE

- If the Administrator should suffer any damage as a result of the User having used the parking lot in a manner that does not comply with these terms, any rules that are indicated at the parking lot, or the User causing damage to any parking facility or equipment through an intentional act or gross negligence, the User shall be responsible for compensating the Administrator for such damage (including the lost operating profit that is caused as a result of the Administrator being required to suspend the operation of the parking lot, in whole or in part, if the situation calls for such measure).

- If the User (the owner of the vehicle and also any passenger riding in the same vehicle) has caused any damage to the parking lot facility, another vehicle being parked, or another User of the parking lot, etc., the User must immediately compensate for the damage by making a proper amount of payment to the party suffering the damage. If the User should fail to report any such incident or make the payment being owed, the case will be reported to the local police.

### ARTICLE 10　UNAUTHORIZED PARKING

- If the User is found to have entered into or exited from a parking space or otherwise exited the parking lot through unauthorized means without paying the parking fee, the Administrator may request the User to pay the parking fee being owed along with the damages, etc., as specified in ARTICLE 9 hereof, etc. For this purpose, the following types of vehicle parking shall be deemed unauthorized:

1. parking of a vehicle over or outside the lines indicating the designated parking space;
2. parking of a vehicle over multiple parking spaces;
3. unpermitted entry or parking of a vehicle into a parking space that has been closed off by the Administrator using safety cones, tape, rope, etc.;
4. parking of a vehicle that is prohibited from using the parking lot pursuant to ARTICLE 5 hereof; and
5. any other act of exiting the parking space or parking lot without settling the parking fee being owed.

### ARTICLE 11　SUSPENSION OF PARKING LOT OPERATION, ETC.

- If any of the following circumstances should arise, the Administrator shall be allowed to suspend the operation of the parking lot, in whole or in part, isolate the parking lot, close off any vehicle path in the parking lot, or evacuate any vehicle (hereinafter collectively referred to as the "Suspension of Parking Lot Operation, etc."):

1. if a natural disaster, fire, damage to an explosive facility or equipment, or any comparable accident has occurred or could possibly occur;
2. if it is deemed necessary to perform any work, cleaning, or sterilization in the parking lot; or
3. if it is otherwise deemed inappropriate to continuously operate the parking lot, etc., due to safety or security reasons.

### ARTICLE 12　CHANGING OF PARKING LOCATION

1. If it is necessary to do so to properly administer the parking lot operation, the Administrator shall be allowed to close any of the entry or exit points or parking spaces.
2. If any vehicle is found to have been parked in the parking lot for more than 48 hours, the Administrator may request the User (including the owner of the vehicle) to move the vehicle from the parking lot, with which the User must immediately comply.


    In such case, the Administrator may lock up the vehicle using chains, move the vehicle to a different location (by tow truck), or take any other action as needed, in order to ensure that the parking lot remains available and safe for normal use.

### ARTICLE 13　ACTION AGAINST ACCIDENTS, ETC.

- If any accident has occurred or could possibly occur, the Administrator may move any concerned vehicle to a different location and take any other action as needed.

### ARTICLE 14　DENIAL OF ENTRY INTO THE PARKING LOT

- If the parking lot is full, the Administrator may deny any additional vehicle from entering into the parking lot. In addition, if any User or vehicle is found to be in breach of any of the rules as set forth in ARTICLE 6 and ARTICLE 7 or otherwise engaged in any prohibited act, etc., the Administrator may deny the User from using the parking lot or force the vehicle out of the parking lot.

## CHAPTER 3　ACTION AGAINST VEHICLES THAT ARE NOT REMOVED FROM THE PARKING LOT DESPITE REQUEST

# Parking Violations

Regulations for illegal parking and other traffic violations became stricter in Japan. If you are found in violation of parking laws, you will be fined a large sum of penalty.

## Do not park in the following places

![주차금지 표시](https://www.timescar-rental.com/images/japan/stop_ph001.png)

The image shows No Parking sign. Do not park the vehicle in the area near this sign.

Rental vehicles must be parked in a parking lot, even if only for a short period of time. Do not park rental vehicles in private parking spaces such as the parking lot or front yard of a private residence. Parking violations are subject to penalties.

On the street

![On the street](https://www.timescar-rental.com/images/japan/stop_ph008.png)In Japan, it is illegal to park on the street even if there is no visible sign which prohibit parkings.

Private property / Monthly parking

![Private property / Monthly parking](https://www.timescar-rental.com/images/japan/stop_ph009_en.png)Do not park in private lands/monthly parkings. This image shows an example of a monthly parking sign.

Parking spaces of convenience stores or restaurants

![Parking spaces of convenience stores or restaurants](https://www.timescar-rental.com/images/japan/stop_ph010.png)Parking spaces of convenience stores or restaurants can be only used if you are using their facilities. You have to move your vehicle immediately when you are finished using the facilities.

![](https://www.timescar-rental.com/images/japan/stop_ic001.png)

If the vehicles is asked to be moved by the land owner or the police as a result of illegal parking, we will collect your rental vehicle and ask you to pay for the moving cost.

## When a parking violation sticker is posted on the vehicle

![When a parking violation sticker is posted on the vehicle](https://www.timescar-rental.com/images/japan/stop_ph002.png)

A sticker similar to the one shown in the image will be posted on the vehicle if you parked in a no-parking area. Do the following steps if a sticker is posted on your vehicle.

- 1Please go to the police station under jurisdiction and receive "Notice of Traffic Violation (交通反則告知書)" and "Payment of Traffic Violation Fine (反則金の納付書).
- 2Please bring the "Payment of Traffic Violation Fine (反則金の納付書)" slip to financial institutions such as banks or post offices and pay the fine.
- 3When you pay the fine, you will receive a "Payment Slip & Receipt (納付書・領収証書等).
- 4When returning the rental car, please present the "Notice of Traffic Violation (交通反則告知書)" and "Payment Slip & Receipt (納付書・領収証書等)" to the staff.

## Parking in Parking Lots

### Lock-style parking lots

#### Parking procedure

![Parking procedure](https://www.timescar-rental.com/images/japan/stop_ph003.png)

1. A locking plate is installed in the center of the parking space.Some can be found at the front part of the parking space.
2. Park the vehicle in an empty space by driving over the locking plate.Do not park in empty spaces with a raised locking plate.
3. Complete the parking procedure within two (2) minutes. Otherwise, the locking plate will automatically be raised.

#### Payment Procedure

![Payment Procedure](https://www.timescar-rental.com/images/japan/stop_ph004.png)

1. Check the number of your parking space.
2. Enter the number of your parking space into the fare adjustment machine. Once you’ve paid the correct parking fee, the locking plate will automatically be lowered.
3. Check whether the locking plate has been lowered before driving out of the parking space.

### Gate-style parking lots

#### Parking Method

![Parking Method](https://www.timescar-rental.com/images/japan/stop_ph005.png)

1. Gate-style parking lots are comparatively larger than other parking lots.Gates are located at the entrance and exit.
2. Stop the vehicle at the entrance gate, press the button on the ticket machine, and then take the parking ticket.
3. Drive into the parking lot. The gate will automatically be raised once you get the ticket.
4. Park the vehicle in an empty space.

#### Payment Method

![Payment Method](https://www.timescar-rental.com/images/japan/stop_ph006.png)

1. Stop the vehicle at the exit gate and insert your ticket into the fare adjustment machine.
2. Pay the parking fee displayed on the fare adjustment machine.
3. Do not reverse the vehicle after paying the fee. The gate will be lowered again if you do, and you will not be able to drive out.
4. Pay the parking fee to open the gate, and then drive out.

## Park Your Car at Times Parking!

![Park in Times pay parking lots.](https://www.timescar-rental.com/images/japan/stop_ph007.png?20190507)

We strongly recommend to park your car at paid parking lots to avoid parking violations.

You can park at Times Parking - Japan's largest car park network!

web.markdown:
Have you ever lost time while driving out because you could not find a parking space? By using coin parking search sites and apps, you can check **availability, fees, and maximum charges** around your destination in advance and park more smoothly. This article summarizes recommended search services and practical tips for keeping parking costs under control.

## What types of coin parking are there? Start with the basics

Coin parking is generally divided into three main types.

- **Lock-plate type**: A lock plate is installed in the parking space and lowers after payment. This is common in smaller parking lots with fewer than 20 spaces
- **Gate type**: A parking ticket is issued on entry and the gate opens. This system is common at large facilities such as shopping centers and hospitals
- **Prepaid type**: You buy a ticket and place it on the dashboard. A single use often costs around 300 to 400 yen, making it relatively affordable

One important point with the lock-plate type is that if you remain parked too long after paying, the plate may rise again, so it is important to **exit promptly after payment**.

## 8 recommended coin parking search sites

### ロケスマWEB

You can search major chains across Japan, including 三井のリパーク and タイムズ. It offers strong features such as **maximum-charge display, route search, and Street View support**, and it also helps you look up nearby restaurants and other destinations at the same time.

### コインパサーチ

You can search in three ways: by area, by free keyword, or by map. With your smartphone’s GPS function, you can **find the nearest coin parking location from your current position with one tap**.

### S-PARK

A search site focused on Tokyo. You can narrow results by conditions such as 24-hour operation, maximum-charge settings, and partner-store discounts. It also supports searches for **Park & Ride (P&R) parking lots**.

### NAVITIME

You can narrow your search to specific chains such as タイムズ and リパーク. It also includes useful travel features such as **reservations, full-lot information, and parking near airports**.

### Parking NAVI

You can search both monthly parking and coin parking. It also allows detailed filtering with **specific conditions such as on-site staff, e-money support, and restroom availability**.

### 特P（トクP）

One of Japan’s largest parking search and reservation services. Many spaces can be reserved for **less than half the typical market price**, and online advance payment also reduces the hassle of settling fees on site.

### SPACE24

A search site specializing in ticket parking. You can search by **options such as support for 1,000-yen bills, 24-hour entry and exit, and transit IC card compatibility**.

### コインパーク駐車場検索

You can search nationwide for parking lots operated by COIN PARK. Results can be filtered by conditions such as **Ponta acceptance, 24-hour operation, and maximum-charge availability**.

## 7 recommended coin parking search apps

- **PPPark！**: Enter your arrival and departure times, and it automatically calculates the cheapest parking option. It also supports reservations and vacancy checks
- **タイムズ駐車場検索**: Real-time vacancy information for タイムズ locations, route search, and fee simulation
- **三井のリパーク駐車場検索**: Real-time vacancy information and support for sending directions to car navigation systems
- **SmooPA**: Cashless payment is available directly in the app. Well suited to parking while traveling
- **akippa**: Search for parking spaces including private spaces, with reservations available up to 30 days in advance
- **Peasy**: Includes a free 30-minute hold feature. Payment is processed automatically on exit using your pre-registered payment method
- **みんちゅう**: A shared parking service that allows unlimited entry and exit within your reserved time

## Apps and services that let you reserve parking in advance

The search sites and apps introduced so far are designed to help you find a nearby open space right now. If you would rather secure a parking spot at your destination in advance, a reservation-based parking-space sharing service is a better fit. Representative services include the following.

- **akippa**: A parking-space sharing service that lets you search and reserve more than 40,000 parking spaces at all times, including private spaces owned by individuals and businesses. Because payment is made in advance, no settlement operation is needed on site on the day of use (according to the akippa official website).
- **特P（トクP）**: One of Japan's largest parking search and reservation services, with many spaces available at prices below the typical market rate, and support for online advance payment.
- **Nokisaki Parking (軒先パーキング)**: A reservation-based parking-space sharing service that matches individuals and businesses with vacant land or unused parking spaces to users looking for a place to park.

Unlike coin parking with an unattended payment machine, these services are distinguished by the fact that they let you reliably secure a parking space only for the time you have reserved in advance. When heading to an area where a full lot is likely, such as around an event venue or during a busy season, it is reassuring to check reservation-based services alongside your coin parking search.

## How real-time availability works, and why some lots don't show it

Most coin parking search services collect data over a network from vehicle-detection sensors and lock-plate status installed at each parking lot, and reflect it on the map as near real-time availability information. Because lock-plate and gate-type coin parking lots can mechanically detect vehicles entering and leaving, the corresponding search sites and apps switch between full and available with only a short time lag. Prepaid (ticket) type lots, on the other hand, are not equipped with sensors that detect entry and exit, so search apps cannot show their availability in real time. A parking lot that should be nearby but does not appear on a search app's map is, in most cases, this prepaid type.

## How can you keep coin parking fees lower?

### Choose a pricing structure that matches your parking time

Parking lots with short-term pricing in 20-minute increments are cost-effective for brief use. If you **use an hourly parking lot for only a few dozen minutes, the cost becomes relatively high**. Estimate your parking time in advance and compare pricing structures carefully.

### Use discounts from partner stores

At parking lots next to department stores or commercial facilities, **several hours of parking may become free** when you shop at or use eligible stores. In some cases, buying gift certificates may also qualify.

### Earn points through cashless payment

If you pay by credit card or e-money, you can earn points. It is also worth using **chain-specific membership services such as Times Club and 三井のリパーク’s Tポイント**.

## Understand how “maximum charges” work and park more economically

Maximum charges generally fall into three categories: **“for ○ hours after parking,” “until 24:00 on the same day,” and “time-band based”**, and each has a different calculation method. If you plan to park for more than four hours, choosing a lot with a maximum-charge setting can significantly reduce your cost. However, if you exceed the stated condition, regular fees will be added, so **check the notes on the sign before using the lot**.

## An owner's perspective: coin parking as a land-use option

For owners who hold vacant land or an unused parking lot, operating coin parking is one form of land use with relatively low vacancy risk. Operating arrangements are mainly divided into three types, depending on how much of the work the owner handles directly (based on Mitsui's Repark (三井のリパーク) official explanation).

- **Self-management**: The owner handles everything, from choosing equipment and setting fees to collecting payments, cleaning, and dealing with problems. Because there is no outsourcing fee, this tends to produce the highest income, but the owner bears the risk of fluctuating occupancy and the burden of day-to-day management.
- **Managed outsourcing**: The owner covers the initial cost, while day-to-day operations are outsourced to a specialist company. This reduces the management burden, but income still fluctuates with the occupancy rate.
- **Full lease (bulk leasing)**: The owner leases the land to an operating company, which covers all initial costs and operational management. This is effectively a land lease, and the owner receives a fixed monthly rent regardless of the occupancy rate.

In terms of profitability, the going rate for a full lease is generally around 1.5 to 2 times what the same land would earn if leased as monthly parking (according to an official column by the parking operator Time Parking (タイムパーキング)). A full lease suits locations where occupancy is hard to predict and stable income is valued, while self-management or managed outsourcing, where there is no ceiling on income, suits well-located sites where the owner is confident of attracting demand. Whichever method you choose, it is important to confirm the conditions for rent revisions and the flexibility of the contract term before signing.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### Q. How many types of coin parking are there?

A. There are three main types: the lock-plate type (common in small parking lots), the gate type (common at large facilities), and the prepaid type (ticket purchase system).

### Q. How can you use coin parking for free or at a discount?

A. If you use partner stores at a neighboring department store or commercial facility, your parking fee may be discounted or waived depending on how much you spend.

### Q. What does maximum charge mean?

A. It is the upper fee limit for a certain period or time band. The longer you park, the more economical it becomes compared with regular pricing. However, the calculation method differs depending on the condition, such as within ○ hours or until 24:00 on the same day, so always confirm the sign before using the lot.

### Q. Can you reserve coin parking in advance?

A. Several services, including 特P, akippa, NAVITIME, and Peasy, support advance reservations. If you want to avoid the risk of a full lot, booking in advance is a practical option.

### Q. What should you do if the lock plate does not go down in a lock-plate system?

A. First, check the operation of the payment machine. The most common cause is entering the wrong parking space number. If that does not resolve the issue, contact the parking lot management company using the number shown on the sign.

# Parking in Japan

## There are acceptable and unacceptable ways to park in Japan.   To avoid parking violations during your travels, please use designated parking facilities, even for short stops.

- 1\. Acceptable parking places
- 2\. Unacceptable parking places
- 3\. How to use coin-operated parking

### 1\. Acceptable parking places

- ### Coin-operated parking

Coin-operated parking lots are conveniently located in various areas, including downtown districts and around train stations, making them an excellent choice for parking during your travels.


Most coin-operated parking lots are marked with a "P" symbol and a sign displaying the parking rates. A 空 or 空車 (open) sign indicates that spaces are available, while a 満 or 満車 (full) sign means the lot is at capacity and you cannot park there.


The most common type of coin-operated parking uses a lock-type system, where a locking plate on the ground secures your vehicle. For larger facilities and commercial complexes, a gate-type system is widely used. In both systems, payment is made after parking. You will pay at a payment machine before exiting.


Parking rates vary by lot, so be sure to check the rate sign or the payment machine.


Additionally, many coin-operated parking lots have a maximum usage limit of 48 hours.


Common signboards at coin-operated parking lots![Coin-operated parking](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/coin_parking01.png)



"Open" and "Full" signage![Coin-operated parking](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/coin_parking02.png)


- ### Parking meters & ticket-based parking

Parking meters and ticket-based parking spots are installed on roads for short-term parking. They are primarily found in designated "time-limited parking zones," which are marked by road signs.


The maximum parking duration is 60 minutes, and you pay a fee by inserting money into the meter after parking.


These zones are intended for short-term parking only, and long-term use like a parking lot is not permitted. Exceeding the time limit will result in a parking violation, so please be mindful of the time.
![Parking meters & ticket-based parking](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/meters_ticket.png)

- ### Parking lots provided by businesses

If the accommodation or commercial facility you are visiting has a parking lot, it is best to use their facilities. It's always a good idea to confirm parking availability in advance.


Also, please refrain from parking outside designated hours, as this is considered a breach of etiquette.


Some facilities may offer parking discounts based on your purchases or use of their services.
![Parking lots provided by businesses](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/businesses.png)


### 2\. Unacceptable parking places

#### Parking in places other than those mentioned above puts you at high risk for incurring a parking violation, so please avoid parking elsewhere.  Please be especially mindful of the following three kinds of places.

- ### Monthly contract parking lots

Monthly contract parking lots are spaces that are rented out on a monthly basis, with users paying a monthly fee. These spaces are already reserved for specific users, so even if a space appears empty, you cannot use it.


To prevent issues, please double-check for 月極 (monthly contract) signs at the entrance or within the parking lot before using it.
![Monthly contract parking lots](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/monthly_parking_lots.png)

- ### Places with specific signage

A red circle with a red diagonal line indicates "No Parking," while a red circle with a red X signifies "No Stopping or Parking."


If there are times written within the sign, it means parking or stopping is prohibited during those hours. For example, if a sign shows "8-20," it means no parking or stopping is allowed between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m.


If no times are specified, parking or stopping is prohibited all day.




\*Even in areas without explicit signs, certain places are designated as no parking or no stopping zones by the Road Traffic Act. For more details, please refer to Articles 44 and 45 of the Road Traffic Act.


No Parking![Places with specific signage](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/specific_signage01.png)



No Stopping or Parking![Places with specific signage](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/specific_signage02.png)

- ### Parking spaces for specialized vehicles

In parking lots at large commercial facilities and highway service areas, spaces may be designated for specific vehicle types. These can include spaces for individuals with special needs, compact cars, large vehicles, or motorcycles.


Parking in a space not designated for your vehicle type is considered a breach of etiquette. Always check for signs indicating specific vehicle designations before parking.
![Parking spaces for specialized vehicles](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/special_parking.png)


- ### ![warning](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/warning.svg)What if you get a parking violation while using a rental car?



**In Japan, enforcement against illegal parking has become stricter. Even short-term parking can result in a violation, so please be cautious.**


If a parking violation sticker is placed on your car, it indicates a parking violation.


You will need to report to the designated police station listed on the sticker and complete the necessary procedures, including paying the fine.


(For example, for an illegally parked standard car, the fine is 15,000 JPY for parking in a no-parking zone and 18,000 JPY for parking in a no-stopping or no-parking zone.)


After handling the violation, please present the documents received from the police station and the receipt when returning your rental car.


If you do not handle the violation before returning the rental car, you will be responsible for paying the parking violation fee set by your rental car company.



![What if you get a parking violation while using a rental car?](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/violation.png)


### 3\. How to use coin-operated parking

#### Lock-type parking

- ### When entering




  - ![When entering](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/locktype01.png)
    Park your car in an available space.

  - ![When entering](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/locktype02.png)
    After a certain period, the lock plate will automatically rise, securing your tires.

  - ![When entering](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/locktype03.png)
    Confirm that the lock plate has risen; your parking is now complete.


- ### When leaving




  - ![When leaving](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/locktype04.png)
    Note the number of your parking space.

  - ![When leaving](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/locktype05.png)
    Enter your space number into the payment machine and complete the payment. Some machines may accept cashless payments, such as credit cards, in addition to cash.

  - ![When leaving](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/locktype06.png)
    Once you confirm the lock plate has lowered, promptly exit the parking space.


#### Gate-type parking

- ### When entering




  - ![When entering](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/gatetype01.png)
    Stop in front of the gate and press the button on the ticket machine to issue a parking ticket.

  - ![When entering](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/gatetype02.png)
    Once you retrieve the parking ticket, the gate will rise.

  - ![When entering](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/gatetype03.png)
    After entering, park in an available space.


- ### When leaving




  - ![When leaving](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/gatetype04.png)
    Stop in front of the exit gate and insert your parking ticket into the payment machine.

  - ![When leaving](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/gatetype05.png)
    The fee will be displayed on the payment machine; proceed with payment. Some machines may accept cashless payments, such as credit cards, in addition to cash.

  - ![When leaving](https://trvimg.r10s.jp/cars/contents/default/images/page/guide_parking/gatetype06.png)
    Once payment is complete, the gate will rise, and you can exit.

# Japan Parking Guide: Apps, Types, and Fee Calculation

![【日本停車場】搵車位 App｜停車位類型 / 停車場種類解說｜泊車收費計算方法](https://www.kwiksure.com/_amplify/image?url=https:%2F%2Fcms-api.primecaremember.com%2Fassets%2Fimages%2FFind-parking-app-JP-820x453.webp&w=1000&h=488&format=webp&q=100)

One of the most vexing issues when [driving a rental car in Japan](https://www.kwiksure.com/blog/self-drive-guided-tour-japan-car-rental-insurance/) is parking! Japan has a wide variety of parking lot types and complex fee structures, and a slight misstep could lead to being "scammed" into paying a high fee. This time, [Kwiksure](https://www.kwiksure.com/) will provide a detailed introduction to common types of parking lots in Japan, methods for calculating fees, and how to easily find an empty spot using a mobile app.

Related Articles

- [2025 Japan Skiing \| Top 10 Popular Ski Resorts, Equipment, and Costs \| Ski Insurance](https://www.kwiksure.com/blog/japan-skiing-guide/)
- [\[Must-read for entering Japan\] Details and precautions on how to use Japan's Joint Kiosk \| Complete entry + customs declaration at one machine \| Applicable to Haneda/Narita/Kansai Airports (with Visit Japan Web tutorial)](https://www.kwiksure.com/blog/visit-japan-joint-kiosk/)
- [\[Travel Internet Guide\] Introduction, advantages, disadvantages, and comparison of 4 internet data plans for overseas travel](https://www.kwiksure.com/blog/travel-internet/)

## Parking Spot Finder Apps

For Hong Kong people driving in Japan for the first time, the first step to finding a parking lot is opening a map. [Google Map](https://www.google.com/maps) is the most direct method; simply enter "駐車場" (parking lot) to see nearby spaces. However, the drawback of Google Map is limited information; it usually doesn't show whether a lot is full, and it may not be able to check if credit cards or electronic payments are accepted.

For Apple iPhone users, [Apple Map](https://maps.apple.com/) also has quite comprehensive information, especially with synchronization with large Japanese parking companies like Times and Mitsui Repark. It can directly show whether a lot is "Full (満)" or "Empty (空)," which payment methods are supported, and can even link to the official app. If you install both apps, you can see fee and availability information on the map.

Android phone users also have many choices, such as [PPPark!](https://pppark.com/), [akippa](https://www.akippa.com/), and [NAVITIME](https://www.navitime.co.jp/parking/). These allow you to view the availability and fees of nearby parking lots in the area and can be sorted by distance or price. However, many lots in PPPark! are privately charged, so users need to pay attention.

[![KS Travel Insurnace 26% Discount](https://www.kwiksure.com/_amplify/image?url=https:%2F%2Fcms-api.primecaremember.com%2Fassets%2Fimages%2F%25E3%2580%258CKS001%25E3%2580%258D%25E5%258D%25B3%25E4%25BA%25AB8%25E6%258A%2598%2520500%25E5%2586%2586FamilyMart%2520%25E9%259B%25BB%25E5%25AD%2590%25E7%258F%25BE%25E9%2587%2591%25E5%2588%25B8.png&w=1000&h=182&format=webp&q=100)](https://api.whatsapp.com/send/?phone=65132112&text=travel888&type=phone_number&app_absent=0)

## Common Types of Parking Lots in Japan

![](https://cms-api.primecaremember.com/assets/images/02-01-08.webp)

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Parking types | Usage and Features |
| Gate-type parking lot | Commonly found in large shopping malls or traditional multi-story/open-air parking lots. The usual practice is to take a ticket upon entry and insert the ticket into the payment machine upon exit to pay and leave. |
| License plate recognition parking | The entrance area is equipped with cameras that automatically record license plates. When leaving, simply enter the license plate number at the payment machine to confirm the amount and make payment. These types of parking lots are often located in large supermarkets or shopping malls, and some customers can waive part of the fee by showing a parking voucher after making a purchase. |
| Ground lock parking lot | Mostly used in small, open-air parking lots, a metal locking plate rises from the center of the ground to lock the vehicle after parking, and is lowered only after payment. Before leaving, remember to check that the locking plate has been released to avoid damaging your vehicle when moving it. |
| Multi-level / lift-type parking garage | This system is commonly used in hotels or commercial buildings, and in some cases, you need to hand over your car keys for staff to operate. When you pick up your car, you show your parking ticket and pay, and the staff will then retrieve the vehicle from the mechanical parking rack. It's safe but more expensive. |

## Japan Parking Space Types

![](https://cms-api.primecaremember.com/assets/images/f6c50fc40409d20714759359f261be62%20(1).webp)

For tourists, hourly parking lots are the most common. However, before parking, you must pay attention to whether the space has the characters "軽専用" (Kei senyō) or "軽" (Kei). This indicates a dedicated parking space for K-Cars (light vehicles under 660cc, with yellow license plates), and you must not park in the wrong spot.

Additionally, there are several types of parking lots you absolutely must not park in to avoid fines or trouble: Monthly rental parking lots (月極駐車場, Tsukigime chūshajō), private corporate parking lots (often marked with "無断駐車禁止" (Mudanchūsha kinshi, No unauthorized parking); violators may be charged high fines), dedicated merchant parking lots without consumption, and areas with "No Parking" signs on the roadside. Also, "無料案内所 P" (Muryō annai-jo P, Free Information Center P) signs, which denote specific facility parking, should not be parked in unless you intend to patronize that facility.

## Parking Lot Fee Structure

![](https://cms-api.primecaremember.com/assets/images/SRB07442.webp)

Japanese parking lot fee calculation is flexible and varied. The most important keyword is definitely "最大料金 (Saida Ryōkin, Maximum Charge/Cap)," which refers to the highest amount payable within a specific period. For example, if it shows "Maximum ¥800 within 12 hours after entry," it means you only need to pay a maximum of 800 Japanese Yen within that 12-hour period. Pay special attention that some parking lots are marked with "一回限定" (Ikkai Gentei, one-time limit) or "繰り返しなし" (Kurikaeshi nashi, no repetition), meaning this maximum charge can only be used once, and after the specified time limit, the charge reverts to the standard rate (hourly); if it says "繰り返しあり" (Kurikaeshi ari, repetition allowed), it means the maximum charge can be repeated, which is suitable for long-term parking.

Furthermore, some maximum charges have time restrictions, for example, only having a maximum charge from evening to morning, with the rest of the time being charged hourly, or only having a maximum charge on specific days like Sundays and public holidays. The maximum charge can also vary depending on the day of the week and time of day, for example, separate daytime maximum charges or nighttime maximum charges.

The hourly rate is another common trap, where many people only pay attention to the first hour's price but overlook subsequent stages. For instance, "First 60 minutes ¥200, then every 30 minutes ¥100" or "Every 15 minutes ¥300," etc. In terms of time units, besides the common hour and half-hour, some parking lots calculate charges based on every 20 minutes or even every minute.

For Hong Kong people unfamiliar with Japanese, it is recommended to take a photo of the fee sign before parking and use Google Translate to confirm terms like "最大料金," "土・日・祝" (Dō/Nichi/Shuku, Sat/Sun/Holidays), and the explanatory text, to ensure you clearly understand the fee calculation method.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How are Japan parking lot fees calculated?

You need to pay attention to the "最大料金 (Saida Ryōkin, Maximum Charge/Cap)" displayed by the parking lot, which refers to the highest amount payable within a specific period. The hourly rate is another common trap, where many people only pay attention to the first hour's price but overlook subsequent stages. In terms of time units, besides the common hour and half-hour, some parking lots calculate charges based on every 20 minutes or even every minute.

### What if I lose my parking lot entry ticket?

You can press the "駐車券紛失" (Chūshaken Funshitsu, Lost Parking Ticket) button on the payment machine or contact the parking lot staff. However, you generally need to pay a penalty equivalent to the parking lot's single-day maximum charge, but the handling process varies depending on the regulations of each parking lot.

## Parking Service

- Times Parking facilities







Times Parking is a generic term for parking provided by Park 24 Group.

- Times Parking Standard







Times Parking Standard is a type of Times parking in which Park24 manages Times parking facilities by renting from individual and corporate landowners idle sites that are unsuitable for buildings and other structures, and using them mainly for small parking facilities.

- Times Parkng Partner







Times Parkng Partner is a type of Times parking in which Park24 rents parking facilities for visitors to commercial facilities, banks, hotels, and government authorities and manages them as Times parking. By making these facilities Times parking, they will be available for anyone to use 24 hours a day. TPS features long-term stable management, as the facilities are rarely diverted to other purposes since they are provided specifically as parking for visitors.

- Parking facility management services







In this business, Park24 provides management services on behalf of hourly and monthly parking facilities operated by hospitals and administrative authorities based on a facility management agreement.

- Times Parking Monthly







Monthly parking lot managed by Park 24 Group

- Times Parking B








A membership service that matches a landowner who wants to utilize idle land effectively with a driver who wants to park his or her car. With an advance reservation on the website, the driver can secure a parking space at his or her destination. With this service, a landowner can lease out a parking space even for just one car or motorcycle, and only while the space is not occupied.


- Park & Charge








Park & Charge is a service to charge electric vehicles provided at Times parking facilities.


- Traffic IC Park & Ride Service








Using this service, users of Times parking automatically receive a preferential fee according to their public transportation use, simply by holding their Traffic IC Card over the fare machine when parking.




※The term “park & ride” means parking a vehicle in a parking space near a train station (“park”) and transferring to a train or bus (“ride”) to alleviate traffic jams and improve the environment in high-traffic areas.

- Times Station








Times Station is a parking building owned by the Park24 Group that is designed to offer multiple Times-branded services.


- Parking Information(Times parking search)








This is a general search site where users can search Times parking facilities across the country from their PC or mobile phone. Users can also set conditions for their search, such as “maximum fee applies” or “electronic money accepted.”



[Back to Top](https://www.park24.co.jp/en/ir/keywords.html#keyword-list)

## Mobility Service

- Times CAR RENTAL







Car rental service developed by Park 24 Group.

- Times CAR







This car sharing service allows users to select cars across the country from "Times CAR" for a minimum of 15 minutes, 24 hours a day, simply by registering for membership.

- RENTAL e Ticket







Complementary electronic tickets can be used for Times Car Rental. Points accumulated with Times Club Cards can be used for Times Car Rental fees when making reservations by following the procedures for converting points into RENTAL e Tickets on the Times Club website.

- CAR SHARE e Ticket







Complementary electronic tickets can be used for Times CAR. Points accumulated with Times Club Cards can be used for Times CAR fees when making reservations by following the procedures for converting points into CAR SHARE e Tickets on the Times Club website.


[Back to Top](https://www.park24.co.jp/en/ir/keywords.html#keyword-list)

## Member Services

- Times Club







Times Club is a membership service with no entry or yearly membership fees. Members can earn points by using services provided by the Park24 Group such as Times Parking, Times CAR RENTAL and Times CAR. Members can then exchange their accumulated points for service usage tickets, goods and other benefits. Additionally, members can take advantage of special deals at a range of affiliated facilities around Japan such as leisure destinations and hotels by presenting their Times Club Card.

- Times Business Card







Corporate-specific card offered by the Park24 Group. The Times Business Card enables cashless payment at Times Parking locations. In addition, Times CAR RENTAL can be used at a special rate for corporate customers, while Times CAR is available without basic monthly fees.


[Back to Top](https://www.park24.co.jp/en/ir/keywords.html#keyword-list)

## Payment Service

- Times Pay








Times Pay is a credit and IC card payment service that is provided mainly in the service industry such as restaurants and retail outlets with the aim of revitalizing destination towns.


Provides three types of devices required for settling - a card reader, mobile printer and tablet.



[Back to Top](https://www.park24.co.jp/en/ir/keywords.html#keyword-list)

## Other

- Road service








Times Road Service quickly dispatches staff to the site of car trouble such as an accident or breakdown to provide various road services including emergency handling and vehicle transportation. Member and non-member services are provided.


- Times Spa Resta








Times Spa Resta is a hot bath facility operated on the 10th to 12th floors of Times Station Ikebukuro.


- Tanoshii Machi (Joyful Town)








This service places free papers bearing information about stores that provide Times Tickets. As signs of affiliated stores are placed inside Times parking facilities, they provide a strong advertising effect, which helps Times parking facilities share customers with these stores.


- Times Ticket








This is a parking service ticket that can be used in Times parking facilities across the country.


Through Times Ticket, Times Parking partners with commercial facilities and other locations that lack parking facilities and provides services to facility users in the form of parking facility tickets.


- TONIC








TONIC stands for Times Online Network & Information Center.


TONIC provides unique system infrastructure for the Park24 Group. By connecting Times services across the country such as parking facilities and car sharing facilities with the information center online, TONIC attracts customers with its streamlined operation and management combined with enhanced customer services.


- Parking Day








Parking Day (August 9) is a commemorative day created in the hope that people will think about their traffic etiquette, recognizing the hazardous nature of roadside parking. Every year around August 9, the Group conducts educational activities aimed at eliminating on-street parking.
